Solution 1 gets the wrong answer: it counts the same handshakes twice.

Witches shake hands only with sorcerers, and sorcerers shake hands only with witches. So every handshake is between one witch and one sorcerer. The total is 6 × 10 = 60.

The solution's 60 already includes every handshake. Its extra 51 "sorcerer handshakes" are the same witch–sorcerer handshakes counted again. It also wrongly subtracts handshakes between sorcerers, even though there were none. So 111 is wrong; the correct answer is 60.

VERDICT: REJECT

Solution 2 is correct. Witches and sorcerers shake hands only with each other, so every handshake has exactly one witch and one sorcerer. Counting by witch gives 6 × 10 = 60. Counting by sorcerer gives 10 × 6 = 60. The two counts agree, and neither counts any handshake twice.

VERDICT: ACCEPT

Solution 3 gets the wrong answer: 30 instead of 60.

It correctly treats each handshake as a pair (Wx, Sy). Counting by witches gives 60, and counting by sorcerers gives the same 60 pairs. These are two separate ways of counting the same set, not two counts to be added together.

The solution never added them to get 120, so there was no double count to remove. Dividing 60 by 2 is therefore an error. Each handshake has exactly one witch and one sorcerer, so the correct total is 6 × 10 = 60.

VERDICT: REJECT
